These latest admissions by Acting Secretary of the Navy Cao that eight sailors assigned to the USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group attempted suicide during this deployment are deeply troubling. My heart is with these sailors, their families, and every service member who has endured the extraordinary strain of this prolonged deployment.

For months, I have been raising concerns about the conditions aboard the USS Lincoln, including inadequate living conditions, insufficient mental health support, and the overall toll this extended deployment has taken on our service members and their families. These latest revelations underscore the urgent need for answers and accountability.

That is why I led a letter to Secretary Hegseth and Acting Secretary of the Navy Cao demanding answers about the conditions aboard the USS Lincoln. I also joined my San Diego colleagues in calling for an independent investigation by the Department of Defense Inspector General. We need to understand how conditions deteriorated to this point, whether our service members received the care and support they needed, and what steps the Navy is taking to ensure this never happens again. Secretary Hegseth and Acting Secretary Cao have yet to respond to either letter.

Our Marines and Sailors have sacrificed so much in service to our country. We owe them more than our gratitude. We owe them the care, support, and resources they need, both during their deployment and when they return home.
